title: A chart-normalized tower pair represents every finite-level test functor
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\ge1$. For a scheme $T$ use the ordinary derived category $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Write $\mathcal C_T$ for its full subcategory whose levels have bounded intrinsically constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, in common intervals independent of $n$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. No normalization is required. At level $n$ write $\mathcal C_{T,n}=D^b_{ctf}(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A_n)$ in the ordinary constant-ring module derived category. For each separated finite-type map $h$ choose a coefficient-independent compactification and write $F_h=Rh_{!,\bullet}$ and $F_{h,n}=Rh_{!,A_n}$ [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $K\in\mathcal C_Y$, and let $G\in\mathcal C_X$ with $\epsilon:F_fG\to K$. Suppose a finite open cover of $X$ consists of coordinate charts $f|_{U_i}=p_de_i$, and that on each $U_i$ there is an isomorphism $G|_{U_i}\simeq e_i^*p_d^*K(d)[2d]$ carrying the restricted counit
$$F_{f|_{U_i}}G|_{U_i}=F_fj_{i!}j_i^*G\longrightarrow F_fG\xrightarrow{\epsilon}K$$
to the sum-then-ordered-integration counit of [lem-sp-tower-coordinate-adjunction]. Let $\epsilon_n:F_{f,n}G_n\to K_n$ be its evaluation through [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Then
$$a\longmapsto\epsilon_nF_{f,n}(a):\operatorname{Hom}(M,G_n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(F_{f,n}M,K_n)$$
is bijective for every $M\in\mathcal C_{X,n}$, naturally in $M$. No assumption that $M$ lifts to a tower is imposed.

Evaluation is triangulated on the ordinary derived categories and preserves the open-extension adjunction maps and restricted counit equations. On a chart the evaluated counit is the finite one; every finite ctf test object, including its open extensions, has an etale-origin representative preserving its Tor interval [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. For any binary open cover $Z=U\cup V$ in $X$, if the restricted evaluated pairs represent the finite functors on $U,V,U\cap V$, the two finite Hom sequences for $A=j_{U\cap V,!}M|_{U\cap V}$, $B=j_{U!}M|_U\oplus j_{V!}M|_V$ have the exact five-term segments indexed by $B[1],A[1],M,B,A$; their outer comparison maps are the finite restricted counit bijections. The same conclusion holds for the empty cover of the empty scheme.

Under the finite adjunction of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] there is consequently a unique counit-preserving isomorphism $G_n\simeq f^!_{A_n}K_n$. For a family of such pairs, any tower morphism whose counit equation is $\epsilon_LF_f(G(u))=u\epsilon_K$ evaluates to the corresponding finite-adjoint morphism. If the family is a tower adjunction, its unit evaluates to the finite unit under these isomorphisms.

source.place: Levels paragraph: evaluation, finite Hom induction and identification with the finite adjoint; agent-stated extraction of the retained nineteen-step proof, steps 13, 14, 15, 16

proof.text: Fix $n$. By [lem-sp-tower-chart-admissibility](1), all schemes and opens used below are Noetherian and qcqs, $A_n$ is finite Noetherian, and $G,K$ are bounded below. The equivalence of [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] supplies an etale-origin representative of every finite ctf object, preserving any specified Tor interval. The actual open adjunction on the finite ctf categories in [lem-sp-open-proetale-counit-scalar] applies with $A=B=A_n$ and the identity coefficient map; in particular open restriction and extension by zero stay in those categories. Thus it applies also to every restricted test object and every extension used below. These are separate finite-level witnesses; no tower of witnesses is chosen.

source.place: Levels: domains of finite test objects and of their open extensions

proof.text: Evaluation is exact by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian](2), hence its termwise derived functor is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Clause (1) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] gives $(F_hC)_n\simeq F_{h,n}C_n$ on the bounded-below inputs here. The actual open adjunction maps and compact-support composition normalizations evaluate to the finite ones by [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus](1),(2). Consequently applying evaluation to the given restricted counit equation gives precisely $\epsilon_{D,n}=\epsilon_n F_{f,n}(j_{D!}G_n|_D\to G_n)$ under $F_{f|_D,n}=F_{f,n}j_{D!}$. This is application of a functor to an equation of morphisms, not detection of equality by evaluations.

source.place: Levels: exact evaluation and preservation of the specified open counits

proof.text: On each given chart $U_i$, evaluate its counit-preserving model isomorphism. By [lem-sp-tower-coordinate-adjunction], evaluation gives the finite chart adjunction, including its sum-then-ordered-integration counit, on all of $\mathcal C_{U_i,n}$. Its domain hypotheses hold by [lem-sp-tower-chart-admissibility] applied to $K$. Hence $\theta^{U_i}_N:a\mapsto\epsilon_{U_i,n}F_{f|_{U_i},n}(a)$ is bijective for every finite ctf $N$, independently of whether $N$ is an evaluation of a tower. When $d=0$ the projection adjunction is the identity, so this includes that case.

source.place: Local pairs and Levels: the evaluated local counit is a finite adjunction counit

proof.text:
For opens $D\subseteq Z\subseteq X$ let $v_D:j_{D!}G_n|_D\to G_n|_Z$ be the open counit and put $\epsilon_{D,n}=\epsilon_{Z,n}F_{f|_Z,n}(v_D)$. Use the finite open adjunction of [lem-sp-open-proetale-counit-scalar] and finite composition normalization of [lem-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-calculus]. If $a:N\to G_n|_D$ has transpose $\bar a=v_Dj_{D!}(a)$, then
$$\epsilon_{Z,n}F_{f|_Z,n}(\bar a)=\epsilon_{D,n}F_{f|_D,n}(a).$$
Thus $\theta^Z_{j_{D!}N}$ is identified with $\theta^D_N$. In particular representability on $Z$ implies it on every further open $D$. This shows that each subopen of a chart has the property of Step 3. Iterated restrictions give the same counit because the composite open counit is $v_Dj_{D!}(v_{D'})$, the composition normalization in the cited calculus.

source.place: Gluing and Levels: identify the comparison maps on open extensions

proof.text:
For a binary open cover $Z=U\cup V$ and $M\in\mathcal C_{Z,n}$ choose an etale-origin representative $L$ by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. Apply the natural signed sheaf short exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-open-cover-shriek-natural-ses] termwise to a complex representing $L$. Its arrows commute with the differential by naturality. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] it gives a triangle with first map the signed overlap inclusions and second map the sum of open counits. Apply exact $\nu_Z^*$, using [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. The open and restriction comparisons, including their actual counits, in [lem-sp-unbounded-open-counit-site-transport] identify its terms and arrows with
$$A\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow M\xrightarrow{\delta}A[1],\qquad A=j_{U\cap V,!}M|_{U\cap V},\quad B=j_{U!}M|_U\oplus j_{V!}M|_V.$$
The overlap inclusions are composites of the same counits, so their signs and their composites are preserved too. Step 1 places all these test objects and their shifts in the finite ctf categories.

source.place: Gluing, repeated after evaluation: the finite signed open-cover triangle; Stacks 0GKK

proof.text:
Write $F=F_{f|_Z,n}$ and $H=G_n|_Z$. By [lem-compact-support-direct-image-triangulated], $F$ carries the triangle in Step 5 to a distinguished triangle, using $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{en}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] to both triangles and their rotations. This gives exact rows
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B[1],H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(M,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(B,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,H),$$
and the row with each $\operatorname{Hom}(T,H)$ replaced by $\operatorname{Hom}(FT,K_n)$. The vertical maps are $\theta_T(a)=\epsilon_{Z,n}F(a)$, including $T=B[1],A[1]$. Every square commutes: for every triangle arrow $t:S\to T$ one has $\epsilon_{Z,n}F(at)=\epsilon_{Z,n}F(a)F(t)$. For $t=\delta$ this uses the shift identification $F(A[1])\simeq(FA)[1]$ in the image triangle. Thus this checks the boundary square as well as the unshifted squares.

source.place: Levels: the exact five-term finite Hom ladder indexed by B[1], A[1], M, B, A

proof.text: Suppose the restricted evaluated pairs on $U,V,U\cap V$ represent their finite functors. Under Step 4 the vertical maps at $A$ and $A[1]$ are the representing maps on $U\cap V$, with tests $M|_{U\cap V}$ and $M|_{U\cap V}[1]$. At $B,B[1]$ they are the direct sums of the maps on $U,V$ with the corresponding tests and shifts; additivity of $F$ and the Hom functors gives these identifications. All four are isomorphisms of abelian groups. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] to the exact ladder of Step 6: its first vertical map is in particular surjective and its last injective. Therefore $\theta^Z_M$ is bijective for every finite ctf $M$.

source.place: Gluing and Levels: finite five-lemma argument

proof.text: Prove the property for every open $Z\subseteq X$ by strong induction on the number $r$ of sets in the restricted given cover $Z\cap U_i$ needed to cover $Z$. For $r=0$, $Z=\varnothing$; module sheaves and their derived objects are zero, and both Hom groups have one element. For $r=1$ use Steps 3 and 4. For $r>1$ let $V$ be the last restricted chart and $U$ the union of the others. Both $U$ and $U\cap V$ are covered by at most $r-1$ restricted charts; their counits are the restrictions of the same $\epsilon_n$ by Step 4. Induction gives the property there, while $V$ is covered by Step 4. Step 7 gives it on $Z$. Taking $Z=X$ proves the claimed bijection. For $b:M'\to M$, the identity $\theta_{M'}(ab)=\theta_M(a)F_{f,n}(b)$ proves naturality in the test object.

source.place: Levels: finite-cover induction, including the empty scheme

proof.text: The finite adjunction used in [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] is the constructible adjunction $Rf_{!,A_n}\dashv f^!_{A_n}$ on $\Dctf$ of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], whose hypotheses hold since $A_n$ is finite and killed by $\ell^n$ and $f$ is separated of finite type. It gives a representing pair $(J,\epsilon^J)$, $J=f^!_{A_n}K_n$, on these same finite ctf categories. Its bijection produces a unique $s:G_n\to J$ with $\epsilon^JF_{f,n}(s)=\epsilon_n$. Step 8 with test $J$ gives a unique $t:J\to G_n$ with $\epsilon_nF_{f,n}(t)=\epsilon^J$. Hence $st$ and $1_J$ have the same transpose under the finite adjunction, and $ts$ and $1_{G_n}$ have the same transpose under Step 8. Injectivity gives $st=1_J$ and $ts=1_{G_n}$. Thus $s$ is the unique counit-preserving isomorphism.

source.place: Levels: identification with the finite right adjoint

proof.text: For a family of pairs and a tower morphism $G(u)$, evaluate its stated counit equation using Step 2 to obtain $\epsilon_{L,n}F_{f,n}(G(u)_n)=u_n\epsilon_{K,n}$. Conjugating by the isomorphisms of Step 9 gives $\epsilon^J_{L_n}F_{f,n}(s_LG(u)_ns_K^{-1})=u_n\epsilon^J_{K_n}$. This is also the defining equation for $f^!_{A_n}(u_n)$, so finite-adjunction injectivity identifies them. Finally, if the family is an adjunction, evaluate its triangle identity $\epsilon_{FM}F(\eta_M)=1_{FM}$. After Step 9 the evaluated $\eta_M$ therefore transposes to $1_{F_{f,n}M_n}$; by the finite adjunction it is precisely the finite unit at $M_n$. This assertion only evaluates units at tower objects; it does not require lifts of arbitrary finite tests.
